newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta share index decline in check.
newsitem.headline: Malta share index decline in check.

text.p: A steep decline in the Malta Stock Exchange share index appeared to have been checked on Wednesday when the index shed only a quarter of a point after losing 18.6 points in the two previous trading sessions.

Turnover on Wednesday reached 452,000 Maltese pounds ($1.2m) compared to 1,991,400 pounds last week, but equities trading picked up with 129,986 shares being transacted compared to only 27,245 a week ago.
Trading in the once-weekly session was spread over 112 deals, of which 49 were in equities and 63 in fixed income securities. The value of the index reached 966.76.
Bank of Valletta dominated equities trading, with 82,992 shares changing hands in 32 deals for an average price of 118 cents per share, down one cent.

There were 15 deals in Mid-Med Bank with 45,890 shares selling for an average of 147.7 cents, up from 146.3 last week. Lombard Bank Malta shares were unchanged, with 1,104 shares being transacted in two deals for 139 cents per share.

Trading in government bonds reached 271,000 pounds. Although 12 issues were dealt in, trading in the 7.25 percent MGS 2006 (II) and the 7.5 percent MGS 2011 accounted for 80 percent of turnover. There were two deals in the 6.5 percent Gasan bonds 1998/99 amounting to 985 pounds and five deals in Mid-Med Bak 7.25 percent unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting to 13,000 pounds. Prices in these bonds remained virtually unchanged since they were last dealt in.
